paragraphs: **Thesis.** A dollar- and price-risk-neutral US equity long/short book. It blends {a:adm.n_admitted|d} literature-signed anomaly signals from {a:adm.n_themes|d} themes with equal theme weights, trades a fraction of the way toward its aim every session, and is costed at $1bn with square-root impact and tiered borrow. On TRAIN 2020-2022 the frozen candidate earns S2 net Sharpe {summ.net_sharpe|+.3f} (gross {summ.gross_sharpe|.3f}, HAC t {summ.hac_t|.2f}) at all-rows gross leverage {summ.mean_gross_leverage_all_rows|.3f}, daily turnover {summ.tau_gmv_mean|.4f} of GMV and a maximum drawdown of {scen.max_drawdown|pct1}.

**What it is not yet.** Everything below is in sample: {a:misc.years|.2f} years, one regime, a cell chosen after {summ.deflated.n|d} NAV cells and many more admission trials. The pre-registered freeze gate asks for a cross-cell deflated Sharpe of at least .95; the cell has {summ.deflated.dsr|.3f} (Lo null {lo.dsr|.3f}). Every step was accepted on the sign of its paired dSR, and each was inside one standard error. End to end against the v5 reference the gain is dSR {a:e2e.dsr|+.3f} (Memmel SE {a:e2e.se|.3f}, t {a:e2e.t|.2f}): suggestive, not established.

**The ask.** Owner decision U1: spend the one remaining validation trial (#3, 2023-2024, book level only) on this single frozen cell, with the read-out rule declared before the read (section 9). Two validation years give SE(SR) of about {a:misc.val_se_2y|.2f}, so validation can falsify the book (net at or below 0) but cannot confirm a Sharpe of 1.
check: The KPI strip and the gate panel read one nav_summ row (N {summ.deflated.n|d}); the appendix recomputes net SR, tau, drawdown and yearly returns from the daily CSV.
Gross-to-net gap: {summ.gross_sharpe|.3f} gross vs {summ.net_sharpe|+.3f} net at {summ.cost_bps_traded|.2f} bps per traded dollar (section 6).

Year split: 2020 {scen.calendar_year_returns.0.net_compounded_return|+pct1}, 2021 {scen.calendar_year_returns.1.net_compounded_return|+pct1}, 2022 {scen.calendar_year_returns.2.net_compounded_return|+pct1}. The Sharpe rests on two years.
The caveats box is part of the pitch, not a disclaimer: each item has a number behind it later in the report.

paragraphs: Every symbol and abbreviation used in this report is defined below, grouped by topic. Scenario keys (S1, S2, S3) name cost scenarios, not Sharpe ratios. "Net" always means after trading costs and financing; "all rows" means a mean over every CSV row including the deployment ramp, which is the basis of the mechanics gate.
A NAV cell's directory name encodes its full construction. The cell-name table below decodes the final cell's name and cross-checks each token against its recipe.
check: Gross leverage is quoted two ways: all rows {summ.mean_gross_leverage_all_rows|.3f} (gate basis) and post-ramp {summ.mean_gross_leverage_post_ramp|.3f} (the L calibration basis).
DSR is quoted two ways: cross-cell {summ.deflated.dsr|.3f} (gate) and Lo {lo.dsr|.3f}; they differ only in the null benchmark SR0.

paragraphs: **Universe.** The research role starts from the top 3000 US listings each session by 63-session dollar ADV (price above $5, ADV above $5M, one-session lag); the base median is {a:univ.base_median|int} members. The linked-operating-v1 restriction then keeps names with exactly one point-in-time issuer link on the primary line, a common share class, and a visible SIC code under 550 days old that is not a pooled vehicle, blank check or royalty trust. It drops {a:univ.dropped_share|pct1} of base member-sessions in the TRAIN window, almost all as unlinked ({a:univ.reason_share.unlinked|pct1}); the kept universe holds {a:univ.kept_min|int} to {a:univ.kept_max|int} names (median {a:univ.kept_median|int}).

**Fields.** {a:fields.n_fields|d} research fields, {a:fields.n_pit|d} flagged point in time. Every finite cell is known by 22:00 UTC on its session date, before the 23:00 UTC decision. Fundamentals (SEC financial statement data) become usable from the first session after the filing's acceptance time plus {a:fields.fund_lag|d} declared lag session; nothing available on or after 2025-01-01 is read. The lowest TRAIN coverage of any field is {a:fields.min_score_cov|pct1}.

**Why the restriction matters.** Before it, about 39% of member cells were ETFs, SPACs and unlinked ADRs that the fundamental signals cannot score, so they were ranked on price signals alone (v6-code-review-signal.md). The restriction was the largest single step of v6 (section 5) and it is also the step with the weakest data foundation (below).
check: Coverage by year (field table): a field that is thin in 2020 cannot carry 2020 alpha.
The identity bridge is a rehearsal (scope_complete {a:univ.scope_complete}); {a:fields.bridge.linked_ciks|int} linked CIKs. Unbridged operating stocks drop out.

Vintage: historical_vintage_verified is {a:fields.historical_vintage_verified}; common_stock_verified is {a:fields.common_stock_verified}. Vendor and FINRA files were downloaded long after their dates.
FINRA short-volume files read: {a:fields.finra_sv_files|int} (sv_ratio126, lag 1 session).

paragraphs: **Design.** Library v6.1 holds {a:adm.n|d} candidates in {a:adm.n_themes|d} themes. Each is one canonical variant of a published anomaly, written in a small expression DSL with the literature sign embedded (higher value = long), so no sign is ever estimated from TRAIN. Firm-level accounting ratios are ranked within FF12 industry. Slow signals are smoothed with a 21-session linear decay of the raw value before the rank; the v5.1 fast sleeves (si_change, ind_adj_rev_5, seasonality_same_month, iv_rv_spread) and sv_flow are not smoothed.

**What three years can say about them.** The median admitted candidate has HAC t {a:adm.median_t|.2f}; {a:adm.n_t_gt_2|d} exceed 2 and {a:adm.n_t_gt_1|d} exceed 1, while {a:adm.n_neg_t_admitted|d} admitted members have a negative t ({a:adm.neg_t_admitted}). This is what an un-mined library looks like on 750 days: individually insignificant signals whose blend has a mean daily rank IC of {a:combined.w5.mean|+.4f} at h 5 (Newey-West SE {a:combined.w5.se|.4f}), positive on {a:combined.w5.pos_share|pct0} of days.

**What changed.** v5.1 to v6 replaced weak or mis-specified members with their stronger published forms and moved smoothing in front of the rank (rank of the decayed value, not decay of the rank); v6.1 added one member, sv_flow (Wang, Yan and Zheng 2020), under its own pre-registration. sv_flow was admitted with HAC t {a:adm.row.sv_flow.hac_t|+.2f} and max |rho| {a:adm.row.sv_flow.max_abs_rho|.2f} (with {a:adm.row.sv_flow.max_abs_rho_with}), so it is not a copy of the short-interest members. The library-changes table lists every change with its cited reason.
check: Decay figure: the combined IC rises with horizon, {a:combined.w5.mean|+.3f} / {a:combined.w21.mean|+.3f} / {a:combined.w63.mean|+.3f} at h 5 / 21 / 63, so the information is slow. The book's theta .05 has a half-life of about {a:misc.half_life|.0f} sessions.
Fast sleeves (standalone tau at or above .08): {a:adm.fast}. They carry {a:adm.fast_weight|pct1} of the composition weight and most of the standalone turnover (turnover vs |IC| figure).
Theme-by-year heatmap: which themes paid in 2020, the weakest year of the book.
The DSL table is verbatim; the words column is a paraphrase written for this report.
Seven candidates (ep, ebit_ev, rd_me, gpa, opbe, fscore, opex_at) are marked insufficient-evidence by the IC runner (IC inference undefined in train_candidates.jsonl); their IC cells read n/a.

paragraphs: **Admission v4-prior-v1 estimates neither signs nor weights.** A candidate is rejected only if it has fewer than {a:adm.rules.min_train_days|d} TRAIN days, standalone turnover above {a:adm.rules.tau_limit|.2f}, a HAC t below {a:adm.rules.veto_t|+.1f} (a clear contradiction of its prior), or a factor-return |rho| above {a:adm.rules.rho_limit|.2f} with a member admitted before it in (tier, roster) order, never in TRAIN-Sharpe order. On lo1: {a:adm.n_admitted|d} admitted, {a:adm.n_redundant|d} redundant, {a:adm.n_veto|d} vetoed ({a:adm.veto}).

**Composition ew-theme-v1** gives every theme with an admitted member the same weight, split equally among its members. The reason is statistical: with about 750 days, estimated means are noise, and sample mean-variance needs thousands of months to beat 1/N (DeMiguel, Garlappi and Uppal 2009). The project learned this directly: v3 used TRAIN-estimated signs and mean-variance weights and went from TRAIN SR 1.81 to validation -1.27 (v6-literature.md, lever X). The one challenger, ew-theme-v6 (drop low_risk, merge options into short_interest, shrink fast sleeves), had paired dSR {@v6l-ew6-t.05-d.1-fixed-obdelta-x.05-loc:parent.dsr|+.3f} (SE {@v6l-ew6-t.05-d.1-fixed-obdelta-x.05-loc:parent.se|.3f}) against its parent: the wrong sign, so it was rejected.

**Diversification.** Admitted signals are weakly correlated: mean off-diagonal cross-sectional correlation {a:sig_corr.admitted.mean|+.3f}, within themes {a:theme_corr.sig_corr.within|+.2f}, between themes {a:theme_corr.sig_corr.between|+.2f}. Daily IC series co-move more ({a:ic_corr.admitted.mean|+.3f} off-diagonal), because a factor-rotation day moves many signals at once.
check: Largest signal pair among all candidates: {a:sig_corr.max_pair} at {a:sig_corr.max|+.2f}; among admitted members: {a:sig_corr.admitted.max_pair} at {a:sig_corr.admitted.max|+.2f}.
Redundancy is measured on factor returns, not on signals, so two members with correlated signals can both be admitted.
Largest member weight {a:adm.max_w|.4f}: a single-member theme gets the full theme weight.
Negative-t admitted members stay in: dropping them on TRAIN t is exactly the selection the protocol forbids.

paragraphs: Construction turns the blended rank signal into dollar positions with one rule, aim-partial-v5, run every session. Levers were added one at a time, each paired against its declared parent and accepted on the sign of dSR only (steps table). The ladder shows the cumulative path from the v5 reference to the final cell.

The book is balanced: mean long {a:expo.long_mean|.3f} and short {a:expo.short_mean|.3f} of NAV, max |net| {a:expo.net_max_abs|.4f}, about {a:expo.held_mean|int} names held. Execution frictions are small: capped fills are {a:fills.capped_share|pct2} of fills, unfilled dollars average {a:fills.unfilled_bps.mean|.1f} bps of NAV per session, and forced nonmember exits are {a:fills.forced_share.mean|pct1} of planned turnover.
check: Mechanics gate: all-rows gross {summ.mean_gross_leverage_all_rows|.3f} (post-ramp {summ.mean_gross_leverage_post_ramp|.3f}), mean net {summ.mean_net_leverage_all_rows|+.4f}, tau {summ.tau_gmv_mean|.4f} / p95 {summ.tau_gmv_p95|.4f}.
L {scen.construction.v5.aim_leverage|g} = 1 / post-ramp gross of the L 1 parent, rounded and declared single-shot before the read; v6.1 kept it fixed.
Held share {summ.held_share|.3f} is above 1: exited nonmembers linger about 60 sessions under exit rate .05 (disclosure D9), and the member-only neutraliser does not hedge them.
Rejected steps (sign against the prior) stay in the table and in DSR N.

paragraphs: **S2, the primary scenario, is a declared, unfitted $1bn cost model.** Every traded dollar pays half-spread {recsc:S2.half_spread_bps|g} bps plus commission {recsc:S2.commission_bps|g} bps, plus square-root impact Y x sigma63 x (|q| / ADV63)^{recsc:S2.impact_delta|g} with Y {recsc:S2.impact_y|g}; fills are capped at {recsc:S2.max_participation|pct0} of 63-day ADV. Financing is a swap (ACT/360): long {recsc:S2.financing.long_spread_bps|g} bps, short {recsc:S2.financing.short_spread_bps|g} bps plus a tier fee of {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.gc|g} (GC), {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.warm|g} (warm) or {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.special|g} bps (special). S1 swaps the trading cost for a flat {recsc:S1.flat_bps|g} bps; S3 writes off names after {recsc:S3.stale_exit_sessions|d} absent session at an adverse haircut.

**Where the money goes** (TRAIN, S2, sums of daily returns): gross {a:costdec.tot.S2.gross_ex_wo|+pct1} of NAV, trading costs {a:costdec.tot.S2.trade|pct1}, financing {a:costdec.fin_share|pct0} of the total drag, net {a:costdec.tot.S2.net|+pct1}. Impact ({a:costdec.tot.S2.imp_bps|.2f} bps per traded $) is {a:costdec.share.impact|pct0} of the drag, the largest component and the one that grows with size.

**Capacity is measured at one point.** Raising L from 1 to 1.247 (+{a:cap.p.V6-U.d_scale_pct|pct0} gross) raised cost per traded $ by {a:cap.p.V6-U.d_cost|.2f} bps, all of it impact; the square-root law predicts {a:cap.p.V6-U.points.1.imp_pred|.2f} bps of impact vs {a:cap.p.V6-U.points.1.imp_bps|.2f} observed. Two points per pair give a local slope, not a capacity curve; AUM above $1bn is untested.
check: Stresses: S1 {scen:S1.net_sharpe|+.3f}, engine-tiers {scen:tiers.net_sharpe|+.3f}, flat-300 {scen:flat300.net_sharpe|+.3f}, S3 {scen:S3.net_sharpe|+.3f} (S3 write-offs {a:costdec.tot.S3.writeoff|+pct1} of NAV).

Borrow mix: GC carries {scen.financing.short_dollar_share_by_tier.mean.gc|pct0} of short dollars, warm {scen.financing.short_dollar_share_by_tier.mean.warm|pct0}, special {scen.financing.short_dollar_share_by_tier.mean.special|pct2}.
Cost per traded $ by year (decomposition table): a jump would signal a liquidity regime the model does not capture.
The spread is a constant 5 bps for every name; small, cheap names are under-charged and large names over-charged.

paragraphs: **Pre-registration.** Every lever set is declared in v4-prereg.md before any TRAIN read of it, and every result goes into the ledger with a cumulative trial count (Appendix A). A step is accepted if the sign of its paired dSR(net) against its parent matches the declared prior; the size is not a criterion, because over {a:misc.years|.2f} years SE(SR) is about {a:misc.sr_se|.2f} (Lo 2002) and no single lever could clear it.

**Paired statistics.** dSR is the difference of annualised net Sharpe ratios on common sessions. Its Memmel (2003) SE uses the correlation of the two return series (rho {summ.paired.rho|.3f} for the v6.1 step, {a:e2e.rho|.3f} end to end vs v5 REF), which is why the paired SE of a one-lever step is an order of magnitude below an unpaired one. A circular block bootstrap (CBB, block 21, 2000 draws) and the Ledoit-Wolf studentized bootstrap give an interval and a p-value. The deflated Sharpe ratio (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014) is computed against two nulls: cross-cell (SR0 from the variance of the N cells' per-session Sharpe ratios) and Lo (variance (1 + SR^2/2) / T of a single cell).

**Why validation #3 is unspent.** The freeze gate needs cross-cell DSR of at least .95 and the cell has {summ.deflated.dsr|.3f}. The controller ruled that no further TRAIN cells are run to move the DSR, since each one raises N; the pre-registered condition binds. Whether to spend validation #3 anyway, with the shortfall disclosed, is the owner's call (U1).
check: N = {summ.deflated.n|d} counts NAV cells only: the admission trials (76 in v6 alone) and the library-design choices are not in N, so the DSR is optimistic on the signal side.
Skew {summ.deflated.skew|+.2f} and kurtosis {summ.deflated.kurtosis|.1f} of daily net returns enter the DSR; fat tails lower it.
TRAIN holds only about {a:misc.nonoverlap63|.0f} non-overlapping 63-session windows.
The appendix trial table quotes each count verbatim from the ledger line it comes from.

paragraphs: The final cell compounds {scen.total_net_return|+pct1} over TRAIN at {scen.ann_vol|pct2} annualised volatility. Its deepest drawdown is {a:dd.rows.0.depth|pct2}, from {a:dd.rows.0.peak} to {a:dd.rows.0.trough}, recovered on {a:dd.rows.0.recovery}; the first figure shows all five cost scenarios with the v6 final and the v5 deployable book for reference.

Daily net returns are left-skewed ({a:rstats.final.daily.skew|+.2f}) and fat-tailed (raw kurtosis {a:rstats.final.daily.kurt|.1f}); {a:rstats.final.monthly.pos_share|pct0} of months are positive and the worst month is {a:rstats.final.monthly.min|+pct2}. 2020 contributes {scen.calendar_year_returns.0.net_compounded_return|+pct1}; 2021 and 2022 carry the result.
check: Rolling 63-session Sharpe: its TRAIN 5th percentile is {a:monitor.roll63.p5|+.2f}, so negative quarters are normal for this book.
Attribution by scenario: gross is almost the same across scenarios; the S1 vs S2 gap is impact.
The {summ.deflated.n|d}-cell table lists every NAV cell that counts in DSR N, with its verdict.
Worst days vs the v5 deployable book: losses on the same sessions point to a shared factor exposure, not to v6 levers.

paragraphs: The risks that decide production are statistical before they are operational. The register pairs each with the TRAIN number that evidences it and the response or open item. The only decision requested now is U1.

**Path to production** if U1 is granted and the read-out is consistent: freeze every pin in the appendix; paper-trade the same NAV engine on live data; track the metrics below against their TRAIN distributions. U2 (pre-2020 history) is the most direct way to shrink the statistical uncertainty; U3 (bridge coverage, delisting returns) and U4 (cost target, AUM) follow.
check: The alarm rules are proposals, not pre-registered tests.

Proposed U1 read-out: "consistent" if validation S2 net is above 0 and the mechanics hold on all rows; the 63-session ramp is about 12% of a two-year window, so post-ramp figures are reported alongside.

paragraphs: Recipe pins per cell, recomputation checks of the headline numbers against the daily CSV, the trial accounting with each count quoted from its source line, and the SHA-256 of every input file the generator read. Regenerate with: `python atx-impl/tools/mega_report --config docs/plans/mega-alpha-v6-pitch.config.json --out docs/plans/2026-09-28-mega-alpha-v6-pitch.html`.
check: Every recomputation check should read MATCH at tolerance {cfg.check_tolerance|g}.
Validation trials spent: #1 (v3) and #2 (v4.1), both at book level; #3 unspent.

list: **Timing.** Mark at session d (data known by 22:00 UTC), decide at 23:00 UTC, fill at the close of d+1; the first return row is d+2.

**Desired weights.** Centred tied rank of the combined signal over the session's members, then price-risk-v1: the OLS residual on [1, beta252 vs the equal-weight market, vol63, log ADV63] (clipped z-scores), rescaled to gross 1.

**Aim and partial step.** aim_i = L x desired_i with L {scen.construction.v5.aim_leverage|g}; next_i = cur_i + theta x (aim_i - cur_i) with theta {scen.construction.v5.theta|g}, unless |aim_i - cur_i| is at most dust / N_d (dust {scen.construction.v5.dust_multiple|g}, N_d members), in which case the name does not trade.

**Delta orders.** The order is the planned change in decision-NAV dollars; price drift between decision and fill rides instead of being traded back. The target basis traded back 17-18% of executed dollars as drift (v6-code-review-exec.md F1).

**Exit rate.** A name that leaves the universe decays as cur x (1 - {scen.construction.v5.exit_rate|g}) per session and snaps to 0 inside the dust band, instead of a forced full exit (19-22% of planned turnover at rate 1, review F2).

**Locate-in-aim.** A member in the special borrow tier with a negative desired weight is set to 0 before neutralisation, so the neutraliser sees the book the broker would allow; {sum.locate_in_aim.zeroed_special_short_aims|int} member-decisions were zeroed.

**Missing prints.** A name that stops printing is carried at its last mark with orders blocked and written off after {recsc:S2.stale_exit_sessions|d} absent sessions (S3: {recsc:S3.stale_exit_sessions|d}, with an adverse haircut).

caveats.title: Honest caveats (read before U1)
items: **TRAIN only.** {a:misc.years|.2f} years, 2020-2022. The 2023-2024 window was read twice at book level for validation trials #1 and #2, never in v6 or v6.1.

**Sign-only acceptance.** Every accepted step had |t| below 1 against its parent. The v6.1 step vs the v6 final: dSR {summ.paired.dsr|+.3f} (Memmel SE {summ.paired.memmel_se|.3f}, t {summ.paired.t|.2f}; CBB 95% {summ.paired.cbb_ci95|+.3f}).
**DSR gate not met.** Cross-cell DSR {summ.deflated.dsr|.3f} is below .95 at N {summ.deflated.n|d} (SR0 {summ.deflated.sr0_annual|.3f} annualised); N counts NAV cells only.

**2020 contributes little.** 2020 is {a:misc.first_year_share|pct0} of the summed yearly returns; the universe restriction lifted 2021-2022 and removed most of the 2020 alpha that the unrestricted role had (the unrestricted loc cell made {@v6l-ew-t.05-d.1-fixed-obdelta-x.05-loc:scen.calendar_year_returns.0.net_compounded_return|+pct1} in 2020).

**Costs are declared, not fitted.** Cost per traded $ rises from {a:cap.p.V6-U.points.0.cost_bps|.2f} to {a:cap.p.V6-U.points.1.cost_bps|.2f} bps between L 1 and L 1.247: impact is convex, so more AUM or more gross loses more.

**Borrow is predicted, not quoted.** Tiers come from public characteristics (market cap, price, short-interest ratio, IPO age). Special-tier short aims are zeroed ({sum.locate_in_aim.zeroed_special_short_aims|int} member-decisions); hard-to-borrow cost may still be understated.
**Identity.** The universe restriction, the largest v6 step, rests on a rehearsal identity bridge (scope_complete {a:univ.scope_complete}).

survivorship.title: Survivorship and look-ahead
items: Membership is point in time (as-of member mask, one-session lag), so names that later delisted are in the panel while they traded.

Delisting returns are not modelled. A name that stops printing is written off at its last mark after {recsc:S2.stale_exit_sessions|d} absent sessions in S2; S3 writes it off after {recsc:S3.stale_exit_sessions|d} session with haircuts long {recsc:S3.terminal_haircut_long|+pct0} / short {recsc:S3.terminal_haircut_short|+pct0} and is the stress for this gap (S3 net {scen:S3.net_sharpe|+.3f}).
The membership recipe keeps the ADV top-N rule as an upper envelope; the linked-operating restriction is applied on top of it.
Nothing available on or after 2025-01-01 is read (the seal is asserted in the fields manifest).

cost_gaps.title: What the cost model does not include
items: Name-level borrow fees and recalls: tiers are predicted (market cap below $1bn, price below $5, SI ratio at least .10, IPO age under one year), not quoted. engine-tiers ({recsc:tiers.financing.tier_fee_bps.special|g} bps special, {recsc:tiers.financing.tier_fee_bps.warm|g} bps warm) is the stress.
Short-sale constraints beyond the special-tier block: no locate failures, no recalls, no short-sale price test.
Closing-auction realism: fills at the close at a modelled cost, with no auction-imbalance or queue model beyond the {recsc:S2.max_participation|pct0} ADV cap.
A constant spread for every name, and an impact coefficient that is declared, not fitted to fills.
No rebate on short proceeds and no interest on cash (excess-return accounting).

one_se.title: What "one SE" means for a three-year window
paragraphs: With T = {a:misc.years|.2f} years, the Lo SE of an annualised Sharpe near {summ.net_sharpe|.2f} is {a:misc.sr_se|.2f}, so its 95% interval runs from {a:misc.sr_ci_lo|+.2f} to {a:misc.sr_ci_hi|+.2f}. Separating 0.74 from 1.0 without pairing would take decades. Pairing near-identical books is far tighter (Memmel SE {summ.paired.memmel_se|.3f} for the v6.1 step), yet every accepted step still had |t| below 1: the evidence for any single lever is its literature prior, not TRAIN.

glossary.def: Primary scenario `modeled-1bn-stale5-v1+swap-fin-v1`: $1bn book; half-spread {recsc:S2.half_spread_bps|g} bps + commission {recsc:S2.commission_bps|g} bps + square-root impact (Y {recsc:S2.impact_y|g}); fills capped at {recsc:S2.max_participation|pct0} of ADV63; write-off after {recsc:S2.stale_exit_sessions|d} absent sessions; swap financing swap-fin-v1.
`linear-6bps-stale5-v1+swap-fin-v1`: a flat {recsc:S1.flat_bps|g} bps per traded dollar, no impact, no participation cap; same financing as S2.

`modeled-1bn-terminal-adverse-v1+swap-fin-v1`: S2 costs, but a name is written off after {recsc:S3.stale_exit_sessions|d} absent session with haircut long {recsc:S3.terminal_haircut_long|+pct0} / short {recsc:S3.terminal_haircut_short|+pct0}; the delisting stress.
S2 trading costs with financing `flat-300-v0`: a flat {recsc:flat300.financing.flat_short_bps|g} bps a year on shorts (ACT/365), no long spread, special shorts not blocked.

S2 trading costs with financing `engine-tiers-v1`: tier fees GC {recsc:tiers.financing.tier_fee_bps.gc|g}, warm {recsc:tiers.financing.tier_fee_bps.warm|g}, special {recsc:tiers.financing.tier_fee_bps.special|g} bps a year.

Swap financing, ACT/360: long {recsc:S2.financing.long_spread_bps|g} bps, short {recsc:S2.financing.short_spread_bps|g} bps plus a tier fee of {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.gc|g} / {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.warm|g} / {recsc:S2.financing.tier_fee_bps.special|g} bps. The tier is predicted per name per decision from public flags (market cap below $1bn, price below $5, SI ratio at least .10, IPO age under 365 days): 0 flags GC, 1 warm, 2 or more special. Special shorts are blocked.
Trading cost dollars (spread + commission + impact) per traded dollar of fills, in basis points.
Annualised Sharpe ratio (x sqrt 252) of daily NAV returns after / before trading costs and financing; excess-return accounting (no cash interest).
t statistic of the mean daily net return with a Newey-West (Bartlett kernel) long-run variance.

Daily one-way turnover in GMV units: sum of |filled dollars| / pre-trade gross, executed fills only, deployment session excluded. Candidate tau (admission) is the same on a candidate's standalone factor.
(long$ + short$) / NAV and (long$ - short$) / NAV averaged over every daily CSV row, including the deployment ramp; the R6' gate basis.
The same means over rows after the first 63 sessions, once the partial-step book has deployed; the basis for calibrating L.
Names held / members; above 1 when exited nonmembers are still decaying out.
Maximum peak-to-trough drawdown of the net NAV.
The construction rule: each session every member moves next = cur + theta x (L x desired - cur), unless inside the dust band (section 5).
Aim leverage, the multiplier on the gross-1 desired book; final cell {scen.construction.v5.aim_leverage|g}.
Trade fraction: the share of the gap between aim and current closed per session ({scen.construction.v5.theta|g}; half-life about {a:misc.half_life|.0f} sessions).
No-trade band multiple: a name trades only if |aim - cur| exceeds dust / N_d ({scen.construction.v5.dust_multiple|g}).
Per-session decay rate of a nonmember's position ({scen.construction.v5.exit_rate|g}); rate 1 is the immediate exit.
Delta: the order is the planned dollar change at decision NAV, so drift rides. Target: the order re-targets the planned weight at fill, trading drift back.
Special-tier short aims set to 0 before neutralisation (v6 prereg C3).

Neutraliser: OLS residual of the tied-rank target on [1, beta252 vs the equal-weight market, vol63, log ADV63], rescaled to the entry gross. price-risk-ind-v1 / v2 add FF12 demeaning (v2 with vol126 / ADV252); both rejected.
The first ~63 sessions, when the book deploys from zero at rate theta.
Information coefficient: the cross-sectional (rank) correlation of a signal at decision d with the forward return close[d+1+h] / close[d+1] - 1; h in sessions (5, 21, 63).
The expression language the alphas are written in (rank, group_rank, decay_linear, delay, ts_sum, correlation, group_neutralize, ...).
Rank of the 21-session linear-decayed raw value vs the decayed rank; v6 moved smoothing before the rank for slow signals and removed it for fast sleeves.
The literature direction; embedded in the DSL (a -1 multiplier where the raw direction is -1), so every candidate's prior sign is +1.
Literature evidence grade A+ to D (replication, post-publication decay, large-cap evidence); orders the redundancy screen.
The composition unit: value, profitability_quality, investment_issuance, earnings_momentum, price_momentum, low_risk, short_interest, reversal_seasonality, options_implied.
A candidate with standalone tau at or above .08.

Admission screen: prior signs, reject on too few days, turnover above {a:adm.rules.tau_limit|.2f}, HAC t below {a:adm.rules.veto_t|+.1f} or |rho| above {a:adm.rules.rho_limit|.2f}; no sign or weight estimation.

Composition: equal weight per theme with an admitted member, equal within theme. ew-theme-v6 (rejected) dropped low_risk, merged options into short_interest and shrank fast sleeves; ew-theme-aim-v1 (v5) weighted by aim gain.
Paired difference of annualised net Sharpe ratios of two cells on common return sessions (S2).
Standard error of dSR under the Jobson-Korkie test with the Memmel (2003) correction; uses the return correlation rho of the two cells.
Circular block bootstrap of dSR: blocks of 21 sessions, 2000 draws, 95% percentile interval.
Ledoit-Wolf (2008) studentized circular block bootstrap test of equal Sharpe ratios; reported as a p-value.

Deflated Sharpe ratio (Bailey and Lopez de Prado 2014): the probability that the true SR exceeds SR0, the expected maximum of N null Sharpe ratios. Cross-cell takes the variance of SR from the N cells; Lo takes (1 + SR^2/2) / T for the cell alone.
N: number of NAV cells counted as trials ({summ.deflated.n|d}); SR0: the deflation benchmark; T: return sessions ({summ.return_rows|d}).
Newey-West SE of a mean daily IC series with lag 2h (overlapping forward returns).
A role is the pinned research panel (sessions x instruments, member mask, prices). Role v2 is the top-3000-by-ADV TRAIN role; lo1 is role v2 restricted by linked-operating-v1.
Universe restriction: one PIT issuer link on the primary line, common class, visible SIC under 550 days old, not a pooled vehicle, blank check or royalty trust (SIC {a:univ.non_operating_sic}).
The lo1 field set: the {a:fields.n_fields|d} research fields (fields-v6b plus sv_ratio126), each with a clock, staleness rule and coverage.
Point in time: a cell's value and whether it is missing use only information available by the decision (22:00 UTC mark, 23:00 UTC decision).
Fama-French 12 / 49 industry groups from the SIC code; used for within-industry ranks and demeaning.
The dated CIK-to-security link table (r4 rehearsal, scope_complete false) that joins filings to listings.
TRAIN = 2020-2022 (all selection and estimation). VAL = 2023-2024, three book-level validation trials in total, two spent. Holdout = 2025 onward, reserved and never read.
Any run whose statistic could influence a choice: each admission candidate, composition, universe and NAV cell. Reproductions with identical bytes are not trials.
The cumulative trial-accounting block every TRAIN result carries in the ledger.
The mechanics gate: all-rows gross in [.90, 1.05], |mean net| at most .02, tau mean at most .20 and p95 at most .30.

alpha_words.value_composite: Mean of the within-FF12 ranks of book-to-market, earnings yield and cash-flow yield (3 of the 4 intended ratios).
alpha_words.bm: Book equity / market equity, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.ep: Trailing net income / market equity, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.cfp: Trailing operating cash flow / market equity, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.fcfp: Trailing (operating cash flow - capex) / market equity, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.ebit_ev: Trailing operating income / enterprise value (market equity + debt - cash), ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.net_payout: Trailing (dividends + buybacks - issuance) / market equity, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.sp: Trailing sales / market equity, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.rd_me: Trailing R&D / market equity, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.gpa: Trailing gross profit / total assets, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.opbe: Trailing operating income / book equity, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.cbop: Cash-based operating profitability: operating cash flow plus R&D (when reported) / total assets, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.roe_q: Quarterly net income / lagged quarterly book equity, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.roa: Trailing net income / total assets, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.accruals: Low accruals: -(net income - operating cash flow) / average assets, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.fscore: Piotroski F-score (0-9 fundamental health), ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.asset_growth: Low asset growth: -(assets / assets a year ago - 1), ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.noa: Low net operating assets / lagged assets, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.issuance_xbrl: Low share issuance: -log of filing share count vs a year ago, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.issuance_vendor: Low composite issuance: -log of split-adjusted vendor shares vs 252 sessions ago, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.sue: Standardised unexpected earnings of the latest filing, ranked.
alpha_words.droe: Change in quarterly ROE vs the same quarter a year ago, ranked.
alpha_words.chtax: Change in quarterly tax expense vs a year ago / lagged assets, ranked.
alpha_words.ear: Market-adjusted 3-session return around the latest earnings announcement, carried forward up to 126 sessions, ranked.
alpha_words.res_mom_12_1: Residual momentum: 12-1 month return net of beta to the equal-weight member market, scaled by residual volatility.
alpha_words.mom_12_1: Return from 252 to 21 sessions ago (12-1 momentum), ranked.
alpha_words.ind_mom_12_1: Mean 12-1 momentum of the stock's FF49 industry, ranked.
alpha_words.within_ind_mom: 12-1 momentum demeaned within FF49 industry, ranked.
alpha_words.bac: Betting against correlation: low correlation of 3-day returns with the market over 250 sessions, ranked.
alpha_words.smax: Low scaled MAX: -(max daily return over 21 sessions / 252-session volatility), ranked.
alpha_words.si_ratio: Low short interest / shares outstanding, ranked.
alpha_words.dtc: Low days to cover (short interest / average volume), ranked.
alpha_words.si_change: Low 21-session change in the short-interest ratio, ranked (fast sleeve).
alpha_words.ind_adj_rev_5: Short-term reversal: -(5-session return demeaned within FF49), ranked (fast sleeve).
alpha_words.seasonality_same_month: Same-calendar-month return one year ago (Heston-Sadka lag 12), ranked (fast sleeve).
alpha_words.iv_rv_spread: 21-day ATM implied volatility minus annualised 21-day realised volatility, ranked (fast sleeve).
alpha_words.opex_at: Operating leverage: (sales - operating income) / total assets, ranked within FF12.
alpha_words.sv_flow: Low long-horizon shorting flow: -(126-session FINRA short volume / total volume, demeaned within FF12), ranked.

change_rationale.value_composite: Composite value averages measurement noise across ratios (Israel, Laursen and Richardson 2021; v6-literature.md section 3.9).
change_rationale.cbop: Cash-based operating profitability subsumes accruals and cfoa (Ball, Gerakos, Linnainmaa and Nikolaev 2016); one variant per hypothesis.
change_rationale.cfoa: Replaced by cbop, which cites the same paper in its stronger form.
change_rationale.res_mom_12_1: Residual momentum has about half the crash risk of raw momentum (Blitz, Huij and Martens 2011); re-trial of the v4.2 candidate.
change_rationale.ind_mom_12_1: Left byte-identical: the member-masked cross-sectional op means the 21-session blackout binds under either smoothing order.
change_rationale.within_ind_mom: Left byte-identical for the same reason as ind_mom_12_1.
change_rationale.bac: Betting against correlation isolates the correlation part of low beta (Asness, Frazzini, Gormsen and Pedersen 2020).
change_rationale.low_beta: Replaced by bac (prereg V6-L); low beta is largely projected out by the price-risk-v1 beta regressor.
change_rationale.smax: Scaled MAX separates lottery demand from volatility (Asness, Frazzini, Gormsen and Pedersen 2020).
change_rationale.low_ivol: Removed: replaced by bac and smax, and spanned by the vol63 neutralisation regressor.
change_rationale.lowvol_ind: Removed: spanned by the price-risk-v1 vol63 regressor.
change_rationale.sv_flow: Long-term shorting flows predict negative returns for about a year; short-term flows do not (Wang, Yan and Zheng 2020); prereg v6.1.
change_rationale._smoothing: Decaying the raw value before ranking removes the 21-session blackout that decay(rank) imposes on names entering the universe, and part of the double smoothing with theta (v6-code-review-signal.md); fast sleeves lose the decay because their alpha is gone within weeks (Da, Liu and Schaumburg 2014).
